question: What is the primary focus of the study of anatomy?

options.A: The physical structures and organization of the body
options.B: The metabolic rate of tissues under physical stress
options.C: The pathological changes caused by infectious agents
options.D: The biochemical pathways operating inside living cells

explanation: Anatomy is strictly dedicated to studying the physical forms, structures, and spatial arrangements of body parts. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why must clinical nurses study physiology alongside anatomical structure?

options.A: To calculate precise dosages based solely on patient weight
options.B: To understand how organs function and maintain life processes
options.C: To memorize the Latin names of every skeletal muscle
options.D: To map out surface markings for surgical incisions accurately

explanation: Physiology explains the active function of biological systems, which is necessary for interpreting clinical symptoms and treatment responses. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h1)

question: What is the basic structural and functional unit of all living human tissues?
explanation: Cells are universally recognized as the foundational building blocks that carry out all vital life processes. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h2)

question: An organ is structurally defined as a combination of which two adjacent organizational levels?

options.A: Multiple chemical molecules bonded by covalent forces
options.B: A collection of identical cells performing identical tasks
options.C: Several distinct organ systems functioning in parallel
options.D: Two or more different tissue types working together

explanation: Organs are composed of various tissue types working in coordination to perform complex tasks that single tissues cannot manage alone. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h2)

question: What term describes the sum of all chemical reactions taking place within the body?
explanation: Metabolism is the overarching umbrella term for both building up and breaking down chemical compounds in living tissue. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h3)

question: Which life process is demonstrated when a patient rapidly withdraws their hand from a painful stimulus?
explanation: Responsiveness involves sensing environmental changes and generating a swift, protective reaction to secure safety. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h3)

question: Which plane divides the body into superior and inferior portions?
explanation: A transverse plane makes a horizontal cut across the body, creating upper and lower halves. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h4)

question: A patient sustained a laceration on the ventral surface of the forearm. Where is this wound located?

options.A: Farther away from the shoulder joint attachment
options.B: On the front or anterior side of the arm
options.C: Closer to the point of attachment to the torso
options.D: On the back or posterior side of the arm

explanation: The term ventral is synonymous with anterior, referring to the front side of the body structure. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h4)

question: Which major muscle separates the thoracic cavity from the abdominopelvic cavity?
explanation: The diaphragm forms the physical anatomical partition between the chest and abdominal cavities. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h5)

question: What is the specific function of the serous fluid found between the visceral and parietal layers of membranes?

options.A: It provides structural rigidity to collapse empty cavities
options.B: It fights off bacterial infections entering from the skin
options.C: It acts as a primary hormone storage reservoir
options.D: It reduces friction as organs move and change shape

explanation: Serous fluid lubricates the membrane layers, allowing organs like the heart and lungs to glide smoothly during contraction and expansion. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h5)

question: What type of feedback loop opposes or reverses a deviation from a physiological set point?
explanation: Negative feedback works to correct deviations and restore stability by moving conditions back toward the normal set point. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h6)

question: Which of the following physiological events is a classic example of a positive feedback loop in humans?

options.A: Insulin release lowering elevated blood sugar levels
options.B: Vasoconstriction to maintain blood pressure during shock
options.C: Shivering to generate heat when body temperature drops
options.D: Uterine contractions during labor and childbirth

explanation: Labor contractions stimulate the release of oxytocin, which intensifies the contractions further until delivery occurs, demonstrating positive feedback. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h6)
